title: Thermistor Failure
fullDescription:
F1 means the microwave cavity thermistor is not reading correctly. The control disables cooking to prevent damage.

Replace the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor in cavity wall.

whenToCallPro: Always recommended due to capacitor risk.

faq.a: No, do not operate with fault.

title: Humidity Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the humidity sensor, used for auto-cook features, is not responding.

You can still use manual cooking mode typically.

title: Keypad Short
fullDescription: F3 is a stuck key fault. A button appears always pressed.

title: Shorted Thermistor
fullDescription: F4 means the cavity thermistor is shorted. Similar to F1 but with shorted reading instead of open.

faq.a: Only if trained with high voltage.

title: Door Switch Fault
fullDescription: F5 indicates the door monitor switch is not operating correctly. Safety prevents magnetron operation.
symptoms: Door appears closed but not recognized

title: Line Voltage Error
fullDescription: F6 indicates voltage supplied is outside acceptable range. Verify outlet and wiring.
whenToCallPro: If outlet is defective, hire electrician.

title: Control Communication
shortDescription: Loss of communication with main board.
fullDescription: F7 is a communication error between control boards. May require board replacement.

title: Fan Motor Error
fullDescription: F8 indicates the cooling fan for the magnetron is not operating. Heat buildup is a risk.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fan motor if dead.

whenToCallPro: If magnetron area work is needed.

title: Turntable Motor Error
fullDescription: F9 indicates the turntable motor is not turning. Food heats unevenly.

title: Magnetron Overheat
fullDescription: F10 indicates the thermal protector on the magnetron has tripped. Overheating has occurred.

faq.a: Often more cost effective if old.
